text: Seabrook Town pulled off an impressive victory against Harbour City, winning 4-2 despite trailing early. Harbour City took the lead with a patient, well-worked goal by Elias Okafor after 17 passes, followed quickly by Marek Barros scoring from a corner cross [#904] [#905] [#973] [#975]. However, Seabrook Town came back strong with Tariq Marlowe scoring off a quick counterattack, showing their direct style [#1103] [#1104]. After a tactical change at 65 minutes, Seabrook Town pressed higher and played more directly, resulting in more chances and goals, including Callum Varga’s goal from a quick 3-pass build-up [#1361] [#1447] [#1448]. In the final minutes, Kian Romano scored twice—both goals coming from quick moves and short, sharp passes—sealing the comeback and the win for Seabrook Town [#1882] [#1906]. Marek Barros shone for Harbour City with 1 goal, 2 assists, and 9 interceptions, but it wasn’t enough to hold off Seabrook Town’s relentless attack [#975].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in en

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals compared to Harbour City's 2, winning the match 4-2. [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906]
- Marek Barros was Player of the Match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and 5 key passes. [#975]
- Harbour City had fewer shots (10) and shots on target (5) than Seabrook Town (22 shots, 9 on target). [team_stats]
- Seabrook Town improved in the second half with a tactical change at 65', increasing press, directness, and line height. [#1361]
- Kian Romano scored 2 late goals including the winning goal at 90+3' with the highest xG of 0.994. [#1882, #1906]

- Harbour City, playing a 4-2-3-1 formation focused on patient short passing, built their first goal through an extended sequence of 17 passes lasting nearly a minute. This demonstrates their methodical build-up style, patiently working the ball forward to find a high-quality chance which Elias Okafor converted from 11.7 meters, assisted by Marek Barros’s through ball [#904, #905].
- Marek Barros also scored a second Harbour City goal immediately after a corner kick with minimal build-up (only 1 pass over 28 seconds), finishing from a cross. This shows Harbour City’s ability to capitalize on set pieces for quick opportunities, despite their usual patient approach [#973, #975].
- Seabrook Town’s formation of 3-4-3 with wide crossing play suits their attacking style, reflected in their comeback starting with a goal from Tariq Marlowe off a rapid counterattack after a defensive ball regain. Marlowe’s goal came with no passes in build-up, highlighting a direct counter-attacking pattern exploiting transitions [#1103, #1104].
- After tactical changes at 65', Seabrook Town pressed higher and played more direct, increasing aggression and line height, which led to more big chances and goals. Their forward line engaged in quick, incisive passing sequences—such as Callum Varga’s goal following a 3-pass build-up from a regain—reflecting effective use of their wide crossing style and formation in a high press [#1361, #1447, #1448].
- Late goals by Kian Romano for Seabrook were scored from quick counterattacks and open play with short, direct passes, illustrating the success of their intensified press and more direct play approach to overturn the deficit [#1881, #1882, #1905, #1906].
